passages.quote:
Overview

Higher technical qualification (HTQ) is a government-backed quality mark. The Department for Education (DfE) awards the quality kite mark to level 4 and level 5 technical qualifications that it has approved against defined approval criteria. Following DfE approval, applicants may use the HTQ quality mark in their promotional and course materials.

These criteria explain how DfE assesses qualifications for HTQ approval.

They set out the requirements qualifications must meet to be recognised as HTQs.

Applicants should read the guidance on applying for HTQ approval, which explains the application process and evidence requirements.

Who the criteria apply to

The criteria are for organisations that manage technical qualifications, including Office for Student (OfS) regulated higher education providers and Ofqual-recognised awarding organisations.

What the criteria cover

The criteria are organised around 5 main areas:

further details on the statutory tests we apply when making an approval decision within the HTQ category

regulation and recognition: qualifications must be recognised organisations and meet any relevant statutory requirements

employer engagement: applications must show employer demand for the qualification and demonstrate employer involvement in its development and review

content coverage: qualifications must demonstrate substantial coverage of the knowledge, skills and behaviours (KSBs) set out in the relevant occupational standard

assessment: qualifications must successfully balance the requirements of:

manageability

validity

reliability

comparability

minimising bias

How the criteria are used

DfE uses these criteria when applying the statutory tests for HTQ approval and making decisions on whether a qualification can be approved and awarded the HTQ quality mark.

HTQ approvals category

Core aim

The qualification:

is at level 4 or 5

aligns to the KSBs in an existing occupational standard

enables entry to the aligned occupation (including providing occupational entry competence with the possibility for further learning or training in work to reach full occupational competence)

Qualifications in this category may be approved under section A2D5 of the Apprenticeships, Skills, Children and Learning Act 2009 (ASCL 2009).

The appropriate tests for this category are:

the alternative approval test (in section A2D5 (3) of the ASCL 2009)

the employer demand test (in section A2D5 (6) of the ASCL 2009)

The alternative approval test is met if:

a standard is published under section ZA11 of the ASCL 2009 for the occupation

DfE is satisfied that by obtaining the qualification a person demonstrates attainment of as many of the outcomes set out in the occupational standard as may reasonably be expected to be attained by undertaking a course of education

The employer demand test is met if DfE is satisfied that there is, or is likely to be, demand from employers in the occupations for employees who have obtained the particular qualification.

How we apply our tests

DfE applies both the alternative approval test and employer demand test to the materials received as part of the applicant’s submission for HTQ approval in order to make an approval decision.

The criteria for approval are laid out in full in this guidance to ensure applicants are aware of the specific focuses of the tests DfE will apply.

DfE also receives feedback from statutory regulators, where relevant, and Skills England when reviewing and approving HTQs.

What you should know before applying

How to apply

Information on how to apply is available in our guidance for applicants.

Level 4 or 5 qualifications you can submit

All qualifications must be validated for delivery before submission.

If submitting higher national qualifications, such as the higher national certificate (HNC) or higher national diploma (HND), you must ensure you have:

received consent from Pearson

submitted evidence of this consent

Submissions into the HTQ category must align to one or more occupations for which an occupational standard is published at level 4 or 5. DfE will only accept submissions of level 4 and 5 technical qualifications in this category. We will not consider any other level of qualification within the HTQ category.

DfE will accept the submission of level 5 qualifications against occupations at level 4. This may be appropriate because qualification content could go beyond the KSBs in the level 4 occupational standard. If your qualification covers both level 4 and level 5 content, level 5 content can be used to map against the level 4 occupational standard.

We do not generally expect to approve level 4 qualifications against occupations at level 5 because it is unlikely that a qualification at level 4 could fully cover the KSBs of a level 5 occupation.

Contact the HTQ team at thtq.contact@education.gov.uk if you have a level 4 qualification that you feel aligns to a level 5 standard and meets all of DfE’s other criteria.

When to apply, including application duration, funding and ‘first teach’

During your pre-application support session, we will discuss with you:

how long your approval may take

when (if approved) your qualification’s ‘first teach’ date would be

Applications are on a rolling basis. DfE no longer sets an annual cut off for funding and ‘first teach’ purposes, as approval timelines will depend on the volume of submissions in progress at that time.

To maximise your chance of a qualification being approved in time for a targeted ‘first teach’ point, we recommend that you submit a clear and complete application as soon as possible.

We analyse applications in the order they are received. However, applications sent back to the applicant for further evidence or clarification may not retain their original place in the processing order. This will be explained to affected applicants.

passages.quote:
u must provide at least one of the following types of evidence to demonstrate that the qualification is in demand and supported by employers:

a survey response from a relevant employer, where they have been asked their opinion of the qualification

reports or comments from employers, industry bodies, think-tanks, professional bodies or combined authorities about skills needs in the occupation or difficulties recruiting

a letter of support from a relevant employer

graduate progression data that shows progression into the aligned occupation

testimony from graduates about their progression from the qualification to the aligned occupation

Employer collaboration and future employer reviews

You must provide the following evidence regarding employer collaboration and regular processes that ensure the qualification continues to fulfil sector needs:

relevant employer membership of forums, boards or committees that discuss qualification development

evidence of amendments to qualifications being made (or considered but rejected for valid reasons) following employer suggestions – for example, a change log

For evidence of employer involvement in the maintenance of the qualification, you must provide at least one of the following types of evidence:

relevant employer membership of forums, boards or committees that discuss qualification development being recurrent

(for new qualifications) plans to involve employers in qualification maintenance

You should ensure you engage with a range of employers relevant to the occupation.

Where an individual or organisation engaged in the development or validation process has a vested interest or conflict of interest (for example, a commercial partnership with the applicant), this should be declared within the evidence submission and, in such circumstances, DfE may seek additional information.

Content coverage (knowledge, skills and behaviours) criteria

All applications to DfE must demonstrate that by obtaining the qualification a person demonstrates attainment of as many of the outcomes set out in the occupational standard as may reasonably be expected to be attained by undertaking a course of education (the alternative approval test).

Knowledge, skills and behaviours

DfE will assess the KSBs in line with the following principles:

Knowledge statements

We expect knowledge statements to be fully covered in the content of the qualification. Exceptionally, we may consider justification of partial coverage – for example, if a specific employer procedure is explicitly referred to in the knowledge statement, meaning that the knowledge could only be acquired when in the workplace.

Skills statements

All standards include skills, where knowledge is actually demonstrated in practice.

Usually, DfE expects skills statements to be fully covered in the content of the qualification. We expect skills delivery facilities that reflect the demands of the occupation, and many skills can be obtained in a peer-to-peer setting, through simulation, scenario or other training device.

You must be specific about how students acquire and demonstrate skills.

Behaviour statements

We would typically expect behaviour statements to be fully covered within a course of education. Where this is not reasonable, we expect a minimum of partial coverage.

For example, if the behaviour statement requires adapting to situations as they arise, we need to see in which module and assessment method this is demonstrated.

Example evidence

Students will learn adaptability skills through role plays and workshop activities [quote modules] and gain a deeper understanding in their practice placement settings. This will be assessed in the role play exercises, evidenced in the personal development and reflection plans.

Some KSBs may only be partially achieved in a course of education. Justifiable reasons include but are not limited to:

that to practice a particular skill, access is required to specialist machinery or equipment, which may not be readily available – however, this should not discourage submission of qualifications that have been designed for specialist providers

the KSB statement requires the individual to be based in an organisation – for example, understanding a particular company’s brand, goals and commercial objectives, or having access to the use of an organisation’s systems or processes

DfE will make a judgement as to whether each KSB (in the occupational standards to which the qualification relates) can reasonably be attained by undertaking a course of education. We may follow this up or request further information where you propose excluding KSBs that we consider could be delivered, either fully, or at least partially, in a course of education.

Qualification pathways and alignment to standards

You must submit one application form per qualification. A qualification can include multiple optional units, modules or occupational pathways.

In qualifications containing more than one pathway, learners can select different module combinations that result in various ‘pathways’ through the qualification. It is common for each pathway to result in separate specialism or deliver into different occupations.

DfE will only approve qualifications where all possible module, unit or occupational pathway combinations cover the KSBs in the occupations to which the qualification relates.

We will not approve qualifications where it would be possible for students to avoid learning certain KSBs, through their choice of optional modules or units, or where a qualification or programme contains occupational pathways of study that are not mapped to an occupational standard or standards in scope for HTQ approval.

Where a qualification aligns to more than one occupational standard, the applicant must make it clear (in the specification) which specific units or modules combine to create each individual qualification or occupational pathway.
